Application Materials.content:
You will need to provide the following documentation as part of your application. This list of documents may vary slightly from course to course.
- **Academic qualifications:** Please provide a transcript for your degree study. If you have not yet completed your degree please provide a transcript of your results achieved to date. If you have completed more than one university qualification, please provide a transcript and certificate for both.
- If your degree was awarded by a UK university, please upload a transcript of your marks for each year or an electronic Higher Education Achievement Reports (HEAR).
- If your degree was awarded by an overseas institution, you should supply a transcript of your marks for each year of your studies and a copy of your degree certificate together with a certified translation if the document is not in English. International and EU applicants are also advised to include high school transcripts.
- We accept copies of physical transcripts and degree certificates as well as electronic transcripts and certificates. Please **do not** submit originals of certificates or transcripts by post.
- If you are submitting copies of physical documents, you should upload clear, colour photographs or scans of your original qualification documents. These documents must confirm that the qualification has been awarded, show the date of the award, and show the final awarded grade.
- **Referee details:** Please provide the contact details of one or two referees on your application as required. You should provide details of an academic referee if you are currently studying, or if you have graduated within the last five years. Professional references may be considered if you have graduated more than five years ago.
- Open references will normally only be accepted if they are written on headed paper, provided as a colour copy of the original, and provide the referee’s work contact details. If you have open references, please upload these at the time of application.
- If you do not have open reference, Queen Mary will contact your referee(s) via email to supply a reference, preferably electronically. A reference provided by email must be sent from a university or company email address; references from a personal email address such as Yahoo or Hotmail are not acceptable.
- Paper reference forms should be endorsed by an appropriate institution/company stamp or on official institution/company letterhead, and should be provided as a scanned colour copy of the original.
- **Statement of purpose:** Your statement of purpose should explain why you want to study your chosen programme and how it will help your future career aspirations. This should typically be one side of A4 paper.
- **Curriculum Vitae (CV)/Resume**
- **English language certificate (if applicable):** If English is not your first language, you should provide evidence of English language ability: IELTS, TOEFL, or other acceptable proof.
- You can still apply even if you haven't yet received your final transcript or your Certificate of English proficiency. Some postgraduate programmes may require applicants to have submitted their Reference letters before a decision has been made.
- Once you have submitted your application, you will have access to the [MySIS applicant portal](https://mysis.qmul.ac.uk/), where you can upload any further documents.

Interview Requirements.content: We don’t conduct interviews for our courses.

Academic Requirements.content:
- The MSc Marketing and Digital Analytics programme is **open to graduates of all disciplinary backgrounds**.
- UK degree requirement: **A 2:2 or above at undergraduate level in any subject**.
- China applicants: Queen Mary normally considers **Bachelor Degree (minimum 4 years) from selected institutions** for entry to postgraduate taught programmes. For a UK 2:2 degree equivalency: **65 to 75%**. Offer conditions will vary depending on the institution you are applying from.

GRE GMAT Requirements.content: No, GMAT is not required for any of the programmes under the School of Business and Management.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
The English language requirements for entry to postgraduate taught programmes in the School of Business and Management falls within the following English band: **Band 4:** IELTS (Academic) minimum score **6.5 overall with 6.0 in each of Writing, Listening, Reading and Speaking**.
The English language requirements for Queen Mary programmes are indicated by English bands, and the specific test and score acceptable is based on the band assigned to the academic department within which the chosen course is administered. Queen Mary accepts a range of English tests and qualifications categorised in its English bands to demonstrate English Language proficiency; see [all accepted English tests](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/international-students/englishlanguagerequirements/accepted-english-language-tests-and-qualifications/) deemed equivalent to these IELTS scores.

Program Overview.content:
The MSc Marketing and Digital Analytics programme is designed to provide insight into marketing and its relationship with the online data economy. Students will develop critical insights into the changing nature of marketing, and learn how to drive campaigns and build consumer relationships within a digital environment. The programme is open to graduates of all disciplinary backgrounds and is also suitable for individuals who are looking to start or develop their own businesses.
- Specialise in data analytics and their use in B2B and B2C marketing, and beyond.
- Examine techniques to measure, track and code human and consumer behaviour.
- Explore the opportunities and challenges within the Big Data economy.
Study options include full-time study starting September 2026 or September 2027, each lasting 1 year. Location: Mile End.
The core modules aim to build foundational knowledge and skills in marketing and digital economy concepts and theories. Broad skills developed during the course include the ability to develop independent insights on marketing in the digital economy; critically evaluate competing approaches and viewpoints, and justify decisions on Big Data and data analytics; review the use of data and its relevance in different cultural contexts; and act ethically and with responsibility in terms of data analytics, with attention to data ethics including data privacy, anonymity and governance.
Structure:
- Seven compulsory taught modules
- One elective module
- Compulsory Dissertation for Marketing or Working with Open Data
Learning outcomes are assessed using a mix of coursework, essays, projects, presentations and, in some cases, exams. There will be variation across modules, and some are wholly examined by coursework. Compulsory dissertation with a choice between Dissertation for Marketing or Dissertation with Open Data.
The teaching team is comprised of Teaching and Research and Teaching and Scholarship staff, complemented where relevant by visiting lecturers with professional expertise in sectors such as communications, advertising and public relations. Students will benefit from this mix of expertise, gaining insights from research, scholarship and industry. Students typically have 3 contact hours per week in each module. Students could take part in a range of different teaching and learning activities, including one-to-one tutorials, guest lectures, simulation game(s), computer-lab based activities, group-work, independent studies, research projects and team learning.
Programme Directors: [Dr Swagato Chatterjee](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/sbm/staff/academic/profiles/chatterjees.html) and [Dr Haytham Siala](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/sbm/staff/academic/profiles/sialah.html). Dr Swagato Chatterjee is Senior Lecturer in Digital Marketing & Analytics and Joint Programme Director of MSc Marketing and Digital Analytics. He has over 9 years of experience in marketing, operations, and analytics and has worked with companies including Coca-Cola, Times of India, Technosoft, Mitsubishi, Nomura, Yes Bank, CSC, Ernst and Young, Godrej, Genpact, and Indian Oil in consultancy and training assignments related to analytics. Dr Haytham Siala is a Senior Lecturer (Associate Professor) in Marketing, specializing in Digital Marketing and Analytics, Technology Enhanced Learning, Digital Healthcare and Digital Well-Being.
Teaching is based at Queen Mary’s [Mile End campus](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/about/howtofindus/mileend/), one of the largest self-contained residential campuses in the capital. Facilities include a ThinkPod interactive collaboration space, Media suite with industry-standard design and editing software (QUBE), Graduate Centre, and 24-hour library on campus.
The School of Business and Management is accredited by the [Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business](https://www.aacsb.edu/about-us)(AACSB). Queen Mary is also part of the [Russell Group](https://russellgroup.ac.uk/).
Graduates of this course will be well-placed to pursue roles in social media management, marketing campaign management, market research, advertising, SEO, CRM communications, marketing analytics or business analytics.

Curriculum.content:
Study options: Full-time, September 2026 | 1 year; Full-time, September 2027 | 1 year. Location: Mile End.
Structure:
- Seven compulsory taught modules
- One elective module
- Compulsory Dissertation for Marketing or Working with Open Data
Compulsory/Core modules:
- Research Methods for Marketing
- Dissertation for Marketing — carries a weighting of 60 credits and involves executing a research plan and independent investigation.
- AI for Business
- Digital Economy, Big Data and Platformization
- Global Marketing and Communications
- Networked and Influencer Marketing
- Brand Storytelling in the Digital Age
- Business Digital Analytics
- Dissertation - Working with Open Data — uses Open Data and the digital analytics taught in the classroom to answer a specific research question.
Elective modules:
- Services Management
- Social Marketing for Social Justice
- Sustainability Marketing, Ethics and CSR
Please note that all modules are subject to change.
Assessment: Learning outcomes are assessed using a mix of coursework, essays, projects, presentations and, in some cases, exams. There will be variation across modules, and some are wholly examined by coursework.
Dissertation: Compulsory dissertation with a choice between Dissertation for Marketing or Dissertation with Open Data.
Teaching: Students typically have 3 contact hours per week in each module. Within these three hours, each module has its own pattern of lectures, seminars/classes and other activities. Students could take part in one-to-one tutorials, guest lectures, simulation game(s), computer-lab based activities, group-work, independent studies, research projects and team learning.

Financial Aid.content:
We offer a number of postgraduate scholarships designed to support both academic excellence and broader access to advanced study.
- **[President's Global Scholarships](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/scholarships/items/presidents-global-scholarships-postgraduate-taught.html)**: The President’s Global Scholarships, offering **£10,000** to highly qualified postgraduate taught offer holders joining us in **September 2026**. Please see the scholarship database for full eligibility.
- **[Global Excellence Scholarship](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/scholarships/items/global-excellence-scholarship-postgraduate-taught.html)**: Worth **£7,000** for high achieving postgraduate taught offer holders joining us in **September 2026/27**. The Scholarship is available to all eligible international students with an offer for an eligible postgraduate taught programme. Please see the scholarship database for full eligibility.
- **[Global Talent Scholarship](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/scholarships/items/global-talent-scholarship--postgraduate-taught-september-2026.html)**: This **£5,000** scholarship supports high-achieving international students enrolling on master’s programmes in **September 2025/26**. You must hold an offer before applying. We also have a Global Talent Scholarships worth **£5,000** for highly qualified postgraduate taught offer holders joining us in **January 2026**. Please see the scholarship database for full eligibility.
- **[Masters Scholarship](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/scholarships/items/masters-scholarships-1.html) (Home Students)**: Available to Home students with an offer for an eligible postgraduate taught programme at the School of Business and Management.
- **Chevening Awards**: We are a proud partner of the UK Government’s Chevening programme, offering fully funded scholarships to students from around the world. These cover tuition fees, living costs and return travel to the UK.
- **Queen Mary Alumni Loyalty Award**: Queen Mary graduates who return for a full postgraduate degree may be eligible for a **10% tuition fee discount**, helping you take the next step in your academic journey.
Use the scholarships and bursaries database to explore funding options: [Search and apply](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/scholarships/database/).

Multiple Applications.content: You may apply for a **maximum of two taught programmes** or **one taught and one research programme** at Queen Mary per application cycle. Please note that you can only study for **one qualification at a time**, so if you receive offers for both programmes you will be required to accept one and decline the other.

Deferral Admission Policy.content: If you wish to defer or withdraw your application, you can do this via the [Applicant Portal](https://mysis.qmul.ac.uk/urd/sits.urd/run/siw_lgn). Simply click on "Request a change" and follow the instructions. Please note you **must have met the academic requirements in order to defer your place**.

Conditional Admission Policy.content: You can still apply even if you haven't yet received your final transcript or your Certificate of English proficiency. You will receive a conditional offer which will state what qualifications and grades you will need to achieve in order to meet our entry requirements. Once you have received evidence of obtaining your qualifications you can upload them to our MySIS Applicant portal after which you will receive an unconditional offer once all conditions have been met. Some postgraduate programmes may require applicants to have submitted their Reference letters before a decision has been made.
